contract: One state sign-off packet per jurisdiction: what changed, what deliberately did not, which legal questions remain open, and the before-and-after terminal for every flow whose outcome moved. Proposals in this file are evidence, not changes.

step1ManifestReconciliation.question: Re-run the audit's generators with --check at this base and reconcile every difference against data/expungement-ai/phase2/correction-allowlist.json before treating it as a defect.
step1ManifestReconciliation.verdict: Every difference is explained by the allowlist. No unexplained difference, so no finding to stop on.

All five already fail at the unmodified base commit, before any change of this shard's, so they are inherited, not caused.

That is allowlist entry 'shared-facts-rendered' exactly, and no terminalOutcome, packetFamily, forms, paymentMode or launchGovernance value moves with it on any retained row.

The only rows that are not simple diffs are Pennsylvania's, and they are allowlist entry 'waiting-rule-recovery-packet-ready': _probe_inside_waiting_period moved needs_review to not_yet, and _probe_state_exclusion_selected moved needs_review to packet_ready_with_caution and now appears twice, once dtc_paid and once partner_sponsored_no_charge, because payment opened. Bounded reachability for this shard's eight: GA not_yet to packet_ready_with_caution and PA needs_more_info to packet_ready_with_caution, both now reaching payment, which is allowlist entry 'ui-reachability-recovered'. WV packet_ready_with_caution to not_yet, which is allowlist entry 'wv-waiting-rule-now-reached' - WV's payment was already closed at the base and is closed now, so nothing sellable moved. AR:situation-a-non-convictions.quote: These are the most accessible filings and generally carry no waiting period.
AR:situation-a-non-convictions.corroboratingQuote: Disposition / offense Waiting period Measured from Acquittal / nolle prosequi / dismissal / arrest None
AR:situation-a-non-convictions.why: This is the only waiting rule the Arkansas pathway itself names, and its text is byte-identical to profile rule wait-01. The § 16-90-1409/1410 non-conviction route has no competing rule: wait-14's own table row for 'Acquittal / nolle prosequi / dismissal / arrest' reads 'None', and wait-03 and wait-13 both state that most Arkansas sealing has no waiting period after the 2019/2021 amendments. No duration is authored here; the value is the one the profile already publishes.

AR:situation-b-misdemeanor-convictions.why: The pathway publishes no waitingRules of its own, and three profile rules compete for the same participant with different durations: wait-14 states 'None' for 'Most misdemeanor convictions and violations', wait-05 states 5 years for 'Certain listed misdemeanors (e.g., negligent homicide, 3rd-degree battery, indecent exposure, public sexual indecency, 4th-degree sexual assault, certain domestic offenses)', and wait-06 states 10 years for a DWI/BWI misdemeanor conviction. Nothing on a rendered Arkansas screen identifies which band a participant is in: offense_level offers only Misdemeanor / Felony / Infraction or violation / Traffic or driving matter / I am not sure, and the one exclusion option that names DUI/DWI routes the participant to likely_not_eligible rather than to a waiting rule. Picking among 0 years, 5 years and 10 years from the offence name would be authoring legal content.

AR:situation-c-felony-convictions.why: A binding is not yet meaningful on this route because the route does not reach the timing gate. Ordered decision rule 'rule-45-and-2021-amendments-the-agent-must-confirm-the-current-' (priority 40, stage timing_and_completion, candidatePathwayIds ['situation-c-felony-convictions']) has an empty when.fieldsReferenced and an empty when.caseOutcomes, so it fires for every participant on this route and returns needs_more_info with frontendAction 'return_to_exact_missing_questions' while missingQuestionIds is empty. Its sourceConditionText is a truncated sentence fragment from the source waiting-periods section ('and 2021 amendments. The agent must confirm the current § 16-90-1405 list and the § 5-4-501(d)(2) violence'), i.e. an instruction to a human agent compiled into a participant-facing decision rule. Correcting it changes an Arkansas evaluator output and so needs a reviewed allowlist entry, which is shared. Separately, the waiting rule itself is not settled: wait-02 states most eligible felonies have no general waiting period while wait-07 states 5 years for a 'Violent Class C / D felony (where otherwise eligible)', and this route's own scope says 'mainly non-violent', so both are live and no rendered field separates them.

KS:conviction-or-diversion-216614.why: Kansas is HELD_FOR_LEGAL_DECISION and this route is why. Its own waiting rule, profile rule wait-01, publishes duration null: 'The form provides offense-dependent one-, three-, five-, or ten-year periods after diversion completion, sentence satisfaction, or discharge from supervision.' The profile states that the period depends on the offence but never states which offence takes which period, so there is no duration in the repository to bind to. wait-02 is a two-year conviction-free condition, not the route's filing wait. Measured at this base with a fully clear record: every one of the eight timing-bucket values, including gt_10_years, returns not_yet with ks.timing_or_completion_blocker, which is the ambiguity being reported rather than a waiting period being applied.

KS:specialty-court-accelerated.why: Kansas is HELD_FOR_LEGAL_DECISION. wait-03 reads 'The form provides a route for a person who successfully completed a specialty court program when the conviction would ordinarily be eligible after three years' — the three years is the period the conviction would ordinarily wait, and this route exists to be reached sooner than that. Binding wait-03 to it would impose the very wait the route accelerates past. The repository does not state what the accelerated period is, so no rule can be bound without authoring one. Measured at this base: not_yet with ks.timing_or_completion_blocker at every timing-bucket value.

KS:drug-registration-relief-coordination.why: Kansas is HELD_FOR_LEGAL_DECISION. This pathway publishes no waitingRules at all and no profile rule names it, so there is nothing to bind. It is automatic true / filingRequired false with suggestedResultCode guidance_only, and it returns guidance_only with ks.guidance_only_no_user_filed_court_petition at every timing-bucket value, which is correct for a route the participant does not file. Absence of a published rule is not the same as a published 'no waiting period' rule, so no_waiting_period may not be inferred here.

OH:adult-conviction-sealing-or-expungeme.why: This route carries nineteen waiting rules whose durations run from 6 months to 10 years, and the rule that governs is chosen by offence degree: wait-05 'minor misdemeanor 6 months', wait-02 'F4, F5, or misdemeanor 1 year', wait-01 '1 or 2 F3 convictions 3 years', wait-08 'felony 10 years after the date the person first becomes eligible to apply for sealing for that felony', wait-03 '2921.43 soliciting improper compensation 7 years'. Ohio's rendered offense_level question offers only Misdemeanor / Felony / Infraction or violation / Traffic or driving matter / Municipal or ordinance matter — it cannot separate a minor misdemeanor from an M1, or an F3 from an F5, and the charge field is postpay. Choosing 6 months over 1 year, or 1 year over 3 or 10, from the answers a participant can actually give would be authoring legal content.

OH:adult-non-conviction-sealing-or-expun.why: Same degree-dependent ambiguity as § 2953.32, with an added conflict of kind: the route is the non-conviction route, yet the rules attached to it are conviction-sealing waits (wait-01 F3 3 years, wait-08 felony 10 years) alongside wait-20, the only genuinely non-conviction rule, which states 'Grand jury no bill 2 years after no-bill report'. Whether a two-year no-bill wait governs an acquittal or a dismissal, and whether any wait binds a non-conviction route at all, is the open question UX-LEGAL-001 records for Ohio. It is a source-law decision, not a configuration one.

OH:certain-firearm-carry-conviction-expu.why: No profile rule names § 2953.35. The route carries the general § 2953.32 degree table plus wait-12, which is the § 2953.39 prosecutor-initiated rule and publishes duration null ('The prosecutor can file after the corresponding 2953.32 waiting period expires'). So the repository points this route back at the § 2953.32 table, which is itself unresolved for the reasons above.

OH:human-trafficking-survivor-conviction.why: No profile rule names § 2953.36. The route inherits the general degree table, and whether a survivor-vacatur route carries the ordinary conviction-sealing wait at all is precisely the kind of question the repository does not answer. Trafficking-survivor relief is commonly available without the ordinary wait, but the repository does not say so for Ohio, and saying it here would be authoring legal content.

OH:human-trafficking-survivor-non-convic.why: No profile rule names § 2953.521, and the route carries the conviction-sealing degree table even though it is a non-conviction route. Both the kind conflict and the degree ambiguity are open.

OH:juvenile-sealing-and-expungement.why: A binding is not yet meaningful because the route never reaches the timing gate: at this base it returns guidance_only with oh.guidance_only_no_user_filed_court_petition at every timing-bucket value, so no waiting rule is consulted. The classification that produces that is isCourtFiledPetitionRoute in src/lib/rcap-engine/evaluator.ts, a prohibited shared path for this shard, while Ohio's own filing instructions describe a juvenile-court filing under §§ 2151.356 / 2151.358. Correct the classification first, then bind. The waiting rule is closer to settled here than anywhere else in Ohio — wait-13 and wait-22 agree on 'five years after the sealing order or upon the person's 23rd birthday, whichever comes earlier' — but that rule is itself two-branch on age, and it presumes a prior juvenile sealing that this route may or may not have, so it needs the legal owner once the route is reachable.

OH:marijuana-hashish-possession-expungem.why: The only rule attached to this route that names § 2953.321 is wait-11, and its content is a hearing-and-fee rule, not a filing wait: 'The hearing must be held 45-90 days after filing; the prosecutor may object ... The filing fee is $50 unless the applicant is indigent.' Binding a 90-day post-filing hearing window as this route's pre-filing waiting period would misstate the rule. Everything else attached is the § 2953.32 degree table. Unresolved.

PA:path-b-complete-acquittal-not-guilty-.anchor: the date of acquittal if the statutory requirements are met
PA:path-b-complete-acquittal-not-guilty-.quote: If the person was acquitted of all charges based on the same conduct or criminal episode, Pennsylvania provides automatic expungement procedures. The statute does not apply to partial acquittals.
PA:path-b-complete-acquittal-not-guilty-.why: wait-01 is the only Pennsylvania rule about acquittal, and this is the only Pennsylvania route about acquittal; the rule's own scope sentence ('acquitted of all charges based on the same conduct or criminal episode', 'does not apply to partial acquittals') is the route's entry condition restated. It governs unconditionally within the route. The same rule is already the first ruleRef of the authored PA:path-a-non-conviction-expungement binding, so this proposal is consistent with what the integration captain has already reviewed for Pennsylvania.

PA:path-c-summary-conviction-expungement.quote: A person may petition to expunge a summary offense conviction if they have been free of arrest or prosecution for five years following the conviction. Pennsylvania law states this summary-conviction expungement pathway is only for summary offenses.
PA:path-c-summary-conviction-expungement.corroboratingQuote: Summary conviction expungement 5 years free of arrest/prosecution
PA:path-c-summary-conviction-expungement.why: Every rule in the Pennsylvania profile that speaks to a summary conviction states the same five years: wait-02 as the operative statement, wait-03 as the agent check ('Check whether five years have passed since the summary conviction'), and wait-14 as the summary table row. There is no competing duration for this route, so the binding is unconditional and no duration is authored.

PA:path-d-ard-expungement.why: No Pennsylvania waiting rule names ARD. The route carries the profile's full seventeen-rule list in default order with no route-specific prefix, which is the compiler's signal that nothing route-specific was found. Whether ARD expungement carries a wait at all, and whether it is measured from ARD completion or from dismissal, is not in the repository.

PA:path-e-age-70-expungement.anchor: final release from supervision or confinement?
PA:path-e-age-70-expungement.quote: Are you 70 or older, and have you had no arrest or prosecution for 10 years after final release from supervision or confinement?
PA:path-e-age-70-expungement.corroboratingQuote: Age-based expungement Age 70 + 10 years arrest/prosecution-free after final release
PA:path-e-age-70-expungement.why: wait-06 and wait-16 both publish 10 years from final release for this route, and no other Pennsylvania rule speaks to it. DEFECT RECORDED WITH THIS PROPOSAL: the third rule in the same group, wait-05, carries duration {value: 70, unit: 'years'} because the compiler read the age threshold ('the person is 70 years of age or older') as a duration. A binding that resolved by longest_bound_duration across wait-05 and wait-06 would therefore impose a seventy-year waiting period. That is why this proposal names wait-06 explicitly and excludes wait-05, and why wait-05's structured duration should be corrected or nulled before any Pennsylvania binding uses a longest-duration disambiguation over this route.

PA:path-f-deceased-person-expungement.quote: Pennsylvania permits expungement when the person has been dead for three years.
PA:path-f-deceased-person-expungement.why: wait-07 is the only Pennsylvania rule about a deceased person and this is the only Pennsylvania route about a deceased person. One rule, one duration, one anchor, no competing candidate.

PA:path-g-underage-drinking-conviction-e.why: No Pennsylvania waiting rule names underage drinking, § 6308, or attainment of age 21. The route carries the full list in default order with no route-specific prefix. Nothing to bind.

PA:path-h-pardon-based-expungement.why: The only place 'pardon-based' appears in the Pennsylvania waiting rules is wait-13, which is not a rule but a bucket enumeration: '[Immediate / 5 years / 7 years / 10 years / age 70 + 10 years / pardon-based / unknown]'. Its structured duration is {0 days, immediate/upon event}, which is an artefact of the compiler taking the first bucket in the list, not a statement that pardon-based expungement is immediate. Binding it would convert a list of buckets into a legal conclusion.

conditions.anchor: conviction for 7 years for offenses punishable by 1+ years, complete restitution, and pay the limited-access fee
conditions.quote: Qualifying misdemeanor or ungraded offense with max penalty no more than 5 years Person must be free from conviction for 7 years for offenses punishable by 1+ years, complete restitution, and pay the limited-access fee
conditions.corroboratingQuote: Eligible M2, M3, or misdemeanor punishable by no more than 2 years Limited access after 7 conviction-free years for offenses punishable by 1+ years and payment of restitution

conditions.anchor: conviction for 10 years for offenses punishable by 1+ years, complete restitution, and pay the limited-access fee
conditions.quote: Qualifying felony Person must be free from conviction for 10 years for offenses punishable by 1+ years, complete restitution, and pay the limited-access fee
conditions.corroboratingQuote: Qualifying offense Limited access after 10 conviction-free years for offenses punishable by 1+ years and payment of restitution

PA:path-i-petition-for-limited-access.why: offense_level is a rendered Pennsylvania screen the participant already answers, and the two rules the compiler prefixed to this route split on exactly that axis: wait-08 for a qualifying misdemeanor or ungraded offence, wait-09 for a qualifying felony. wait-10 and wait-11 restate the same split with the same conviction-free counts, so all four candidates agree. Both durations are the ones the profile already publishes. NOT COMPLETE: 'Traffic or driving matter' and 'I am not sure' select no rule. Neither may be defaulted to the misdemeanor branch — a summary traffic offence is a different remedy in Pennsylvania, and 'I am not sure' is the absence of a fact, which the evaluator's existing missing-fact path should continue to handle. Those two values are for the legal owner.

PA:path-j-clean-slate-automatic-limited-.why: The only Clean Slate rules the Pennsylvania profile publishes are about summary convictions: wait-04 'Clean Slate may also automatically seal some summary convictions after five years' and wait-15 'Clean Slate summary sealing 5 years after judgment + restitution'. This route is not limited to summary convictions, and the profile publishes no Clean Slate period for the misdemeanor band it also covers. Binding the summary five years to the whole route would understate the wait for part of it, which is the shape of error the release rule exists to prevent.

PA:path-k-human-trafficking-vacatur-expu.why: No Pennsylvania waiting rule names trafficking, vacatur, or § 9122.4. Nothing to bind.

WV:no-conviction-expungement-for-acquitt.anchor: the court's order of acquittal or dismissal
WV:no-conviction-expungement-for-acquitt.quote: Timing: the petition may be filed no sooner than 60 days after the court's order of acquittal or dismissal. ("https://code.wvlegislature.gov/61-11-25/")
WV:no-conviction-expungement-for-acquitt.why: wait-01 is the § 61-11-25 timing rule and this is the § 61-11-25 route; the rule states one period, from one named anchor, with its statutory citation. West Virginia's own filing instructions restate it: 'file a civil petition in the circuit court where the charges were filed, no sooner than 60 days after the acquittal/dismissal order'. wait-02 (pretrial diversion agreements 'generally may not exceed 24 months') and wait-03 (deferred adjudication 'can last up to three years for a felony and up to two years for a misdemeanor') are the lengths of the programmes, not waits before filing, and the filing instructions confirm the diversion route still files on the dismissal order. Nothing is authored: the duration and the anchor are the profile's own.

WV:eligible-conviction-expungement-under.why: The profile states the source plainly — 'These waiting periods are directly set by 61-11-26(b)' — and publishes all three: wait-12 'Single misdemeanor 1 year', wait-13 'Multiple misdemeanors 2 years', wait-14 'Nonviolent felony 5 years'. The rule that governs turns on whether the participant has one misdemeanor or more than one, and no rendered West Virginia screen asks that: offense_level offers only Misdemeanor / Felony / Infraction or violation / Traffic or driving matter / I am not sure, and criminal_history is a postpay packet field. A conditional binding on offense_level would resolve 'Felony' to wait-14 but would have to guess between 1 and 2 years for every misdemeanor participant, so it is not proposed. Adding a rendered single-versus-multiple conviction-count question would make this bindable, and that is a shared-flow change, not a shard change.

WV:accelerated-treatment-recovery-job-re.why: The § 61-11-26a table has the same three-way shape and the same missing selector: wait-05 'Single misdemeanor After sentence/supervision completion and 90 days of approved treatment/recovery compliance or job-readiness completion', wait-06 'Multiple misdemeanors 1 year', wait-07 'Eligible nonviolent felony 3 years'. Single versus multiple is not asked, so the misdemeanor branch cannot be resolved without guessing between 90 days and 1 year.

WV:first-offense-drug-possession-conditi.why: West Virginia's filing instructions describe a six-month waiting-period calculation for the § 60A-4-407 conditional-discharge route, and the pathway carries a clause reading '4 Six-month waiting-period calculation.' — but no West Virginia waitingPeriodRules entry publishes a six-month structured duration. The three rules that could carry it (wait-11, wait-15, wait-16) all have duration null; wait-16's entire ruleText is the string 'not_eligible_yet_waiting_period'. Writing six months into a binding would be authoring the duration, because the profile does not publish it. The right fix is to compile the six-month rule into this jurisdiction's waitingPeriodRules with its source quote, and then bind it.

WV:juvenile-record-relief.anchor: the juvenile's 18th birthday, or one year after personal or juvenile jurisdiction ends, whichever is later
WV:juvenile-record-relief.quote: West Virginia juvenile proceeding records are generally not public records. One year after the juvenile's 18th birthday, or one year after personal or juvenile jurisdiction ends, whichever is later, juvenile records may be kept in a separate secure confidential place and may not be inspected except by circuit court order. ("https://code.wvlegislature.gov/49-5-104/")
WV:juvenile-record-relief.why: wait-10 is the only West Virginia rule about juvenile records and this is the only West Virginia juvenile route; the rule carries one duration, one named anchor and its statutory citation. This is the route the Phase 2 allowlist entry 'wv-waiting-rule-now-reached' names as reporting that it cannot execute its waiting rule now that disposition_date is asked, so this proposal is the direct answer to that recorded gap. The 'whichever is later' clause is a max over two anchors of the same one-year duration, not a choice between two durations, so the binding stays unconditional.

WV:pardon-based-expungement.anchor: being pardoned and five years after discharge of the sentence for the pardoned conviction
WV:pardon-based-expungement.quote: A person is not eligible until one year after being pardoned and five years after discharge of the sentence for the pardoned conviction. Pardon-based expungement is not available for first-degree murder, treason, kidnapping, or felony sex offenses under Article 8B. ("https://code.wvlegislature.gov/5-1-16A/")
WV:pardon-based-expungement.why: wait-09 is the only West Virginia rule about a pardon and this is the only West Virginia pardon route. It is a single published rule with a single structured duration and its citation. Note for the reviewer: the rule is conjunctive — one year after the pardon AND five years after discharge — and the profile's structured duration captures only the one-year limb, with the five-year limb inside the anchor string. The binding is still unconditional because there is one rule and no competing candidate, but the evaluator will apply the shorter limb unless the five-year limb is also compiled as structured data. That is a compilation gap in the profile, recorded here rather than papered over.

WV:sex-trafficking-victim-vacatur-and-ex.why: No West Virginia waiting rule names § 61-14-9, trafficking, or vacatur. The pathway's rule list is the profile's whole list in default order with no route-specific prefix. Nothing to bind.

UT:path-a-automatic-clean-slate-expungem.why: Utah is HELD_FOR_LEGAL_DECISION: 'The waiting rule for these routes cannot be settled from repository content. Choosing one would author legal content, so none is authored and none is guessed.' This shard preserves that and records rather than resolves. On its own terms the route is also unresolved: Clean Slate periods are published per offence class (wait-06/wait-20 'Class C misdemeanor or infraction 5 years', wait-07/wait-21 'Class A misdemeanor controlled-substance possession 7 years'), and Utah's rendered offense_level cannot express a Utah offence class.

UT:path-b-automatic-expungement-after-ac.why: Utah is HELD_FOR_LEGAL_DECISION. The route's own rule wait-04 publishes two different periods for the two outcomes it covers — 60 days after acquittal, 180 days after a qualifying dismissal with prejudice — and case_outcome does distinguish those two answers, so a conditional binding is arguably within reach. It is deliberately not proposed: the hold says none is authored and none is guessed, and wait-02's carve-out 'unless dismissed after plea in abeyance' is a third branch that no rendered Utah screen can express. Recorded for the legal owner as the Utah route closest to bindable.

UT:path-c-clean-slate-eligible-convictio.why: Utah is HELD_FOR_LEGAL_DECISION. Offence-class-dependent Clean Slate periods with no rendered selector, plus the plea-in-abeyance carve-out that wait-02 and wait-19 both exclude from the automatic route.

UT:path-d-petition-based-expungement-wit.why: Utah is HELD_FOR_LEGAL_DECISION. The two rules the compiler prefixed to this route are process rules, not filing waits: wait-08 'File the petition in the correct Utah court within 180 days of certificate issuance' and wait-09, the BCI response time. The actual periods are the petition table (wait-22 Class C/infraction 3 years, wait-23 Class B 4 years, wait-24 Class A 5 years, wait-25 felony drug possession 5 years, wait-26 felony generally 7 years, wait-27 misdemeanor DUI 10 years) and it is selected by Utah offence class, which no rendered screen supplies. Measured at this base: not_yet with ut.timing_or_completion_blocker at every timing-bucket value.

UT:path-e-petition-based-non-conviction-.why: Utah is HELD_FOR_LEGAL_DECISION. The route's own rule wait-10 publishes duration {30 days} but its ruleText is a description of who may petition ('If the person was arrested or charged but not convicted, Utah may allow petition-based expungement of records of arrest, investigation, and detention'), and the 30 days sits in an anchor string that is a truncated list of statutory outcomes rather than a period measured from a named event. Binding a 30-day wait off that text would be reading a duration the rule does not state. Measured at this base: not_yet with ut.timing_or_completion_blocker at every timing-bucket value.

UT:path-f-petition-based-conviction-expu.why: Utah is HELD_FOR_LEGAL_DECISION. The petition table is offence-class-selected with six competing durations from 3 to 10 years and no rendered selector. Recorded alongside it: this route is typed court_filing but returns guidance_only with ut.guidance_only_no_user_filed_court_petition at every timing-bucket value, so it never reaches the timing gate at all. Both the classification and the rule are for the legal owner; neither is this shard's to move while Utah is held.

UT:path-i-traffic-offense-expungement-or.why: Utah is HELD_FOR_LEGAL_DECISION. Four rules and four different periods for one route: wait-16 '3 years after adjudication or dismissal for Class C misdemeanor/infraction traffic cases and 4 years for Class B', wait-34 'Traffic petition No BCI certificate; 3 or 4 years depending level', wait-35 'Traffic automatic deletion 5 or 6 years depending level', wait-15 5 years. The route covers both the petition and the automatic-deletion remedy, which have different periods, and the level split is not askable on a rendered screen. Measured at this base: not_yet with ut.timing_or_completion_blocker at every timing-bucket value.

UT:path-j-cannabis-possession-petition-w.why: Utah is HELD_FOR_LEGAL_DECISION. UT:path-k-pardon-based-expungement.why: Utah is HELD_FOR_LEGAL_DECISION. No Utah waiting rule names a pardon or the Board of Pardons and Parole waiting period. Nothing to bind, and the route returns guidance_only with ut.guidance_only_no_user_filed_court_petition at every timing-bucket value.

UT:path-l-vacatur-human-trafficking-rela.why: Utah is HELD_FOR_LEGAL_DECISION. No Utah waiting rule names § 77-40a-402, vacatur or trafficking. UT:path-m-juvenile-expungement.why: Utah is HELD_FOR_LEGAL_DECISION. waitingRuleDispositionSummary.contract: A proposal is evidence, not a change. src/lib/rcap-engine/waiting-rule-bindings.json and src/lib/rcap-engine/evaluator.ts are prohibited to this shard and neither was touched. No duration in this file was written by this shard: every one is quoted from the duration the jurisdiction's own compiled profile already publishes, with its rule id.
waitingRuleDispositionSummary.method: A route earns EXPLICIT_BINDING_PROPOSED only when one published rule governs it with no competing candidate inside the route's own scope. Where the governing rule turns on a fact a rendered screen already collects, and the answer values are nameable, it earns EXPLICIT_CONDITIONAL_BINDING_PROPOSED, with any answer value that selects no rule listed as unresolved rather than defaulted. Everything else is LEGAL_OWNER_DECISION_REQUIRED, which the release rule makes the correct answer over a guess. HELD_FOR_CORRECTION is used only where the route does not reach the timing gate at all, so a binding could not take effect if it were made.

defectsFoundInWaitingRuleData.severity: would impose a seventy-year waiting period
defectsFoundInWaitingRuleData.detail: PA wait-05 carries duration {value: 70, unit: 'years'}. Its ruleText is 'Pennsylvania permits expungement when the person is 70 years of age or older and has been free of arrest or prosecution for 10 years following final release from confinement or supervision.' The compiler read the age threshold as a duration. The actual period is 10 years and is published correctly by wait-06 and wait-16.
defectsFoundInWaitingRuleData.consequence: Any binding over the age-70 route that disambiguates by longest_bound_duration - which is the disambiguation the eleven authored bindings in waiting-rule-bindings.json use - would select 70 years. The authored PA:path-a-non-conviction-expungement binding does not list wait-05 in its ruleRefs, so it is not affected today.
defectsFoundInWaitingRuleData.recommendation: Correct or null wait-05's structured duration before any Pennsylvania binding uses longest_bound_duration over path-e.

defectsFoundInWaitingRuleData.severity: a bucket list compiled as a rule with a zero duration
defectsFoundInWaitingRuleData.detail: PA wait-13's entire ruleText is '[Immediate / 5 years / 7 years / 10 years / age 70 + 10 years / pardon-based / unknown]' and it carries duration {value: 0, unit: 'days', raw: 'immediate/upon event'} because the compiler took the first bucket. It is an enumeration of the buckets a reviewer picks from, not a rule.
defectsFoundInWaitingRuleData.consequence: A shortest-duration or first-match disambiguation over any Pennsylvania route would read it as 'no waiting period'.
defectsFoundInWaitingRuleData.recommendation: Exclude wait-13 from every Pennsylvania binding, or drop it from waitingPeriodRules.

defectsFoundInWaitingRuleData.severity: a conjunctive rule with only one limb compiled
defectsFoundInWaitingRuleData.detail: WV wait-09 states two conditions - one year after the pardon and five years after discharge of the sentence - but publishes duration {1 year}, with the five-year limb surviving only inside the anchor string. An evaluator reading the structured duration applies the shorter limb.
defectsFoundInWaitingRuleData.consequence: The proposed WV:pardon-based-expungement binding is still correct as the only pardon rule, but it will under-apply the wait until the second limb is compiled.
defectsFoundInWaitingRuleData.recommendation: Compile the five-year limb as structured data before the binding goes active.

defectsFoundInWaitingRuleData.severity: three rules with no rule in them
defectsFoundInWaitingRuleData.detail: WV wait-11's ruleText is 'Conviction category Waiting period' (a table header), wait-15's is 'These waiting periods are directly set by 61-11-26(b). (' (a truncated citation), and wait-16's is the bare string 'not_eligible_yet_waiting_period' (a reason code). All three have duration null.
defectsFoundInWaitingRuleData.consequence: The § 60A-4-407 six-month period that West Virginia's own filing instructions describe has no compiled home, which is why WV:first-offense-drug-possession-conditional-discharge-relief cannot be bound.
defectsFoundInWaitingRuleData.recommendation: Compile the six-month rule with its source quote and drop the three non-rules.

defectsFoundInWaitingRuleData.severity: an instruction to a human agent compiled into a participant-facing decision rule
defectsFoundInWaitingRuleData.detail: See AR-DEFECT-001. Priority 40, stage timing_and_completion, empty when.fieldsReferenced and empty when.caseOutcomes, so it fires unconditionally on situation-c-felony-convictions and returns needs_more_info with frontendAction 'return_to_exact_missing_questions' while missingQuestionIds is empty.
defectsFoundInWaitingRuleData.consequence: Arkansas's felony route cannot reach a terminal decision, and the participant is returned to a screen with nothing on it to answer.
defectsFoundInWaitingRuleData.recommendation: Remove it or convert it to an internal review flag, with the correction allowlist entry proposed below.

openLegalQuestions.question: Utah's three packet-producing routes (paths D, E and I) are blocked by a waiting rule the repository cannot resolve, and its eight other routes never reach the timing gate at all. openLegalQuestions.measuredAtThisBase: Paths D, E and I return not_yet with ut.timing_or_completion_blocker at every one of the eight timing-bucket values. Paths A, B, C, F, J, K, L and M return guidance_only with ut.guidance_only_no_user_filed_court_petition at every value. For A, B and C that is correct - they are automatic true routes a participant does not file. For F, J, K, L and M it is not obviously correct: they are typed court_filing, pardon_then_court, special and juvenile respectively, and Utah's own filing instructions describe court filings for several of them.
